comparator.sourceNotes: The selected Spanish and Latin American Studies abroad pathway closes 60+60+60. It keeps the required 30-EC Spanish/Latin American university semester separate from 30 EC of genuine free profiling, and counts the 12-EC Spanish-language thesis once. Abroad entry requires at least 54 first-year EC plus attendance in year-two semester one; part-time exchange starts no earlier than year three. An unweighted home alternative is not stacked. Diagnostic test and recurring tutoring are mandatory zero-credit formation. Current course evidence supports Dutch, Spanish and English instruction.

alternatives.concept: Study literature, empire, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media and language/power across transatlantic and global contexts. Treat these as related humanities and social-science approaches while preserving the absence of Spanish-language proficiency and a sustained Spain/Latin America sequence.

alternatives.labelRationale: The label names the completed curriculum’s literature, empire, migration, media, heritage and cultural-memory content without claiming Spanish-language study or a full Spain/Latin America curriculum.

alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal cultural production. Preserve Spanish proficiency and Spanish-specific linguistics as explicit gaps.
basisLabels: Spanish-language and Latin American literature, media, cultural sources and textual interpretation

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film and media; it is labelled as cultural-expression study and not as Spanish proficiency or Spanish linguistics.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Native American Histories, European Union Politics and three art/heritage courses are replaced by Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication, Creative Communication Laboratory and From T.V. to TikTok. The change shifts advanced study from colonial histories, heritage and cultural memory to language, rhetoric and mediated expression.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; the only formal prerequisite, Introduction to Brain & Behavior for Psycholinguistics, occurs two semesters earlier. alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third Spanish-proficiency, translation and source-language programme is not feasible because the workbook contains no Spanish acquisition sequence, advanced Spanish grammar, sociolinguistics, translation or Spanish-language academic writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as Spanish proficiency.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: UCR explicitly studies bilingualism and language acquisition, giving a limited direct relationship to multilingualism. Its cognitive/neurobiological approach does not supply Spanish proficiency or the external course's Spanish-specific social and linguistic diversity.
Both analyse linguistic form and meaning; UCR uses stylistics and literary linguistics rather than a general introduction to linguistics within Spanish studies.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Español 1.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Español 2.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Español 3.
UCR has no Spanish-language acquisition sequence corresponding to Español 4.
Psycholinguistics and stylistics do not reproduce the programme’s Spanish-language linguistic perspective.
UCR has no advanced Spanish-language acquisition corresponding to Español 5.
UCR has no advanced Spanish-language acquisition corresponding to Español 6.
UCR has no Spanish-Dutch translation course or sustained Spanish translation practice.
Both establish literary analysis and interpretation; UCR is a general literary-studies course rather than Spanish-language literary study.
Both introduce literary traditions and interpretation; UCR spans a broad canon and does not supply Spanish proficiency.
Both analyse culturally situated narratives, identity and otherness; UCR is cross-cultural rather than focused on Spain and Latin America.

The limited regional overlap is UCR's explicit study of Latin American civil-sphere and civil-repair cases within contemporary social theory. The external course covers a much broader regional agenda, including race/ethnicity, development, extractivism, violence and human rights; UCR does not provide that regional survey.
The programme’s broad humanities introduction remains part of the external curriculum and is not forced into a one-course equivalence.
UCR courses address identity and institutions in several contexts but do not reproduce this programme-specific philosophy-of-science component.

A general modern-history survey supplies background but the course evidence does not establish substantial history of Spain or Latin America. The Spanish-speaking-world component therefore remains separate.
The required 30-EC Spanish/Latin American university semester has no scheduled UCR equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC profiling space remains open and is not equated with scheduled UCR courses.
The compulsory Spanish-language thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study global literature, colonial and postcolonial histories, migration, cultural memory, heritage, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and language/power. UCR does not offer Spanish proficiency progression, Spanish grammar and sociolinguistics, translation, Spanish-language academic writing, or a cumulative Spain and Latin America literature/culture sequence, so these are related humanities routes rather than Spanish Language and Culture equivalents.
